correctness.rationale: Full-rank Gaussian projected columns yield an exact flat-spectrum Nyström projector identity. The leave-one-out basic residual has a \(\chi^2_1\) law. Conditional on the other \(k-2\) columns, two remaining projected Gaussian columns live in a two-dimensional plane and their squared residuals have joint mean \(3/2\) from the exact \(\sin^4\) angular moment \(3/8\), giving covariance \(1/2\). This proves the rank-\(k\) variance \(a^2(k+3)/(2k)\), expected spread proxy \(3a^2/(2k)\), and correlation \(1/4\), for every \(k\ge2\). One more probe makes each leave-one-out span full rank. The \(k=2\) Laplace transform follows from independent \(\chi^2_4\) lengths and a \(\operatorname{Beta}(1/2,1/2)\) angle. All calculation and scope boundaries were checked; 479 numerical diagnostics passed.

originality.rationale: The primary FlexTrace analysis proves estimator-level bounds but does not calculate the flat-rank Gaussian pair moment. XNysTrace Proposition 3.1 already gives a general correlation-dependent calibration identity, and Proposition 5.3 gives a broad variance bound; the exact correlation \(1/4\), finite-rank variance coefficient, \(k\)-dependent proxy ratio, and rank-crossing one-probe transition require the independent conditional two-dimensional calculation shown in the proof. No covering result appeared in the checked records, although unindexed Gaussian regression identities remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: The result may be implicit in unindexed classical joint Wishart/projection-residual identities; the single-coordinate inverse-Wishart law is known.

The earlier general posterior-error identity is strictly stronger as a formula conditional on the actual pairwise correlation; novelty is only the exact spectral-model correlation and its consequences.

value.rationale: A new exact reliability benchmark isolates a rank-critical failure of the standard leave-one-out squared-error diagnostic: its expected value decreases as \(1/k\) even though the actual absolute MSE stays at least \(a^2/2\), while one additional probe completely removes the error. The precise phenomenon is a motivated issue for sample-budget decisions and uncertainty calibration in function-of-matrix trace estimation, rather than a rote simplification of the estimator. The result does not extrapolate to relative-error failure or arbitrary matrices.
